title: Morning Edition
dek: A global bond selloff pushed U.S. borrowing costs to a 24-year high; companies are struggling to scale AI beyond pilots; Greece's Lake Koroneia has nearly vanished; and a new Ontario festival builds a local tradition around Black culture.

lead_story.headline: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2002
lead_story.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.3% as a global bond selloff intensified, extending a sharp quarterly rise even after softer U.S. inflation data.
lead_story.why_it_matters: Treasury yields feed directly into borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt and government finance; a sustained move above 5% changes the financial backdrop even without another immediate Federal Reserve move.

items.headline: Most companies still cannot move AI projects beyond the pilot stage
items.summary: A BearingPoint study found only 13% of surveyed companies were on track with AI initiatives. Nearly three-quarters reported positive financial results, but fewer than a third had moved beyond pilots.
items.why_it_matters: The bottleneck in enterprise AI is increasingly implementation rather than proof of value: regulation and integration with legacy systems are slowing deployment.

items.headline: Lake Koroneia has shrunk to less than a tenth of its former area
items.summary: The northern Greek wetland has contracted from about 34.4 square kilometres in 2016 to 2.7 square kilometres amid low rainfall, higher evaporation and continued irrigation pressure.
items.why_it_matters: Koroneia shows how warming, drought and local water use can compound each other, turning climate change from an abstract trend into a rapid landscape-scale loss.

items.headline: Scientists built a cell-by-cell map of gene activity across the human prefrontal cortex
items.summary: The PsychAD consortium analyzed more than 6.3 million cells from 1,494 donors ranging from infancy to age 108, mapping how gene activity changes across development, aging and several neurodegenerative diseases.
items.why_it_matters: The atlas gives researchers a common reference for linking genetic risk and disease biology to particular brain cell types rather than treating the cortex as a single tissue.

items.headline: Chile intercepted more than 200 ammonite fossils in a shipment declared as decorations
items.summary: Customs officials found the roughly 110-million-year-old fossils in a container from China; packaging pointed toward Madagascar, whose government was asked to help establish their origin and possible repatriation.
items.why_it_matters: The seizure is a small window into the international trade in scientifically valuable fossils and the practical problem of returning natural heritage to its place of origin.

items.headline: Rockwood is starting a harvest festival around Black culture and community
items.summary: The inaugural Calabash Harvest Festival in Rockwood, Ontario will bring together steelpan, West African drumming, storytelling, food, beading, pumpkin carving and local vendors on October 10.
items.why_it_matters: It is the kind of modest local institution that can become tradition simply because a community decides to make room for it every year.
items.source: EloraFergusToday / Wellington County Black Heritage Society

items.headline: What happens when a society treats optimization as a default virtue?
items.summary: A recent essay on play argues that activities governed by scores, streaks and measurable outcomes can crowd out forms of experimentation whose purpose emerges only while doing them.
items.why_it_matters: The argument reaches beyond games: it offers a way to ask whether productivity tools and metrics sometimes destroy the unmeasured activity from which curiosity and new purposes arise.

worth_your_time.headline: Black holes ring like bells, and the fading signal leads into the information problem
worth_your_time.summary: An Aeon essay follows the measurable ringdown after black-hole mergers into the deeper question of whether information that crosses an event horizon is destroyed, hidden or recoverable.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: It uses an observable physical signal as a path into one of the deepest unresolved conflicts between relativity, quantum theory and information.
